pr_title: Fix Culture Native and Display Names
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/53362

This change is fixing the wrong behavior of the Culture Native and Display names. We had the following behavior:
- Display names were cached which is wrong. The display names should be treated as the localized resources and should be retrieved every time using the CurrentUICulture.
- There is some old special case for supplemental culture which is not applying anymore because Windows already using supplemental culture LCID values for some of its built-in cultures. 
- When requesting the native or display names using ICU, if ICU couldn't find a suitable resource for the request, it just return the culture name e.g. `en-US instead of English (United States) ` which is not suitable to use in the UI apps.

The fix here is doing the following:

- For display names now, we use CurrentUICulture to retrieve the name.
- Removed the supplemental culture special case. 
- When requesting the display and native names from ICU, we fallback to English names if couldn't find resources for the requested culture. 
- Added some test

issue_context.title: [.NET 5] Proper DisplayName in CultureInfo "aa" missing
issue_context.body:
### Description

`CultureInfo` for `aa` (Afar) does not contain a proper `DisplayName` nor the `NativeName`. Both fields contain only `aa`.

**Reproduce:**

```csharp
var aa = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo( "aa" );
```

**Expected Behaviour**

```csharp
aa.DisplayName == "Afar"
aa.NativeName == "Qafaraf"
```

**Actual Behaviour**

```csharp
aa.DisplayName == "aa"
aa.NativeName == "aa"
```



### Configuration

* Framework: `net5.0-windows10.0.19041`
* Platform: Windows 10 20H2
* Arch: x64
* Local culture: reproducible with German and English system


### Regression?

+ in .NET Framework 4.8: `aa.DisplayName == "Afar"`
+ in .NET 3.1: `aa.DisplayName == "Qafar"`


Cheers,
Georg

review_comments: Why do these tests need RemoteExecutor?

I want to have Current UI culture always be set in isolated execution environment. This to void resetting it every time we use it. The other reason I want to restrict the test to the platforms support remote execution as ICU in other environments are trimmed and I expect the ICU there will not have all needed resources we depend on.
I removed the remote execution from the tests and I'll let CI tell if this will succeed.

> I want to have Current UI culture always be set in isolated execution environment. This to void resetting it every time we use it.

What's the problem with resetting it every time we use it?  We use the ThreadCultureChange helper in tons of tests:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/01b7e73cd378145264a7cb7a09365b41ed42b240/src/libraries/System.Globalization/tests/NumberFormatInfo/NumberFormatInfoCurrentInfo.cs#L25-L28
There's an issue with using it here?  To be clear, my concern is simply that the remote execution stuff adds considerable overhead, and we've culled back usage of it to only the cases where we really do need a clean slate where we fully control everything that gets run... I'm not clear why this falls into that category (if it does, though, ok).

> I removed the remote execution from the tests and I'll let CI tell if this will succeed.

Ah, great, thanks!

@stephentoub 
I am wondering about the behavior of the `ThreadCultureChange` if the execution code inside the using scope throw exception. does the dispose will get a chance to execute and restore the original cultures?
The original check was checking `DefaultThreadCurrentUICulture`, but we are no longer checking that. Is that intentional?
Yes, that is right. The old logic was wrong especially for Windows. We should always check `CurrentUICulture` instead.
